summary: HelixBank: ordered-response gap and connection saturation causing streaming disconnects and duplicate messages
description:
Issue summary:
HelixBank experienced a production outage window beginning 2026-03-11 08:42 UTC where streaming connections observed ordered-response gaps (responses arriving out of expected order), intermittent duplicate messages, and abrupt disconnects. Customer impact: endpoint latency spikes, degraded UX for live chat use-cases, and elevated error rates (5xx/stream disconnects).

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat sessions saw ~22% of streaming sessions report at least one disconnect or duplicate message during the 30-minute window.
- Automated reconciliation on HelixBank side retried and triggered rate spikes, causing sustained elevated load.
- Incident risk: potential SLA breach for HelixBank (enterprise/dedicated).

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: ded-helixprod-us-east (GPU-backed dedicated capacity).
- API gateway version: 3.7.2; Streaming service: realtime-v1.14; Serving runtime: redwood-runtime-2.3.0-rc4.

Observed behavior / reproduction steps:
1) Open a streaming chat session against HelixBank's pinned model redwood-chat-v2 in prod-us-east.
2) Send a multi-part prompt (system + user + user follow-up) with partial flushes to trigger streaming chunks.
3) Observe that chunk ordering occasionally flips (later chunk delivered before earlier one) and some connections disconnect with HTTP/2 RST_STREAM or grpc CANCELs.
4) In parallel, note increased 5xx rates and connection re-establish attempts from the client.

Initial mitigation performed:
- Support activated emergency throttle on HelixBank service route at 09:10 UTC to stabilize incoming rate.
- Rolling restart of a subset of dedicated serving nodes in ded-helixprod-us-east at 09:24 UTC to free memory pressure.
- Temporarily disabled prefix-KV caching for the affected route as a diagnostic at 09:30 UTC.

Why this ticket exists:
This is a customer escalation and post-incident follow-up to capture timeline, root cause analysis, and action items to prevent recurrence. The customer requested a formal write-up and confirmation of configuration changes and timeline for a permanent fix.

investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: memory fragmentation / slow GC in runtime causing per-connection buffering anomalies; evidence: heap growth and GC pause spikes on affected nodes (see trace node-7, node-11).
Hypothesis B: network-level packet reordering on a subset of NICs producing out-of-order gRPC frames (low probability) — NIC team ran pcap and found no hardware-level drops.

Hypothesis C: KV cache eviction race where cached partial response fragments were re-emitted during replays leading to duplicates; disabling KV cache reduced duplicates but did not remove ordering gaps.
Heap/Garbage Collector: nodes showed 2x baseline GC pause time for a 7-minute window coincident with error peak. Kernel tunables for net.core.rmem/wmem were unchanged.
Serving runtime instrumentation: kvcache miss ratio increased before incident; then nodes hit >90% open FD count which correlated with RST_STREAM.

workaround: Applied short-term throttling on the HelixBank route and rolled a subset of serving nodes to clear memory pressure. Disabled prefix-KV caching for the route. These measures reduced duplicates and stabilized ordering while patch work progressed.
resolution: Root cause: an interaction between aggressive prefix-KV caching and memory/FD exhaustion in a subset of dedicated serving nodes. Under high client retry patterns, nodes reached elevated open-FD counts and GC pause spikes which disrupted streaming chunk ordering and led to RST_STREAM disconnects. Fixes applied: (1) runtime patch to add backpressure and lower FD thresholds, (2) KV cache safety guards to avoid re-emitting partial fragments during reconnection, (3) autoscaler tuning for faster scale-up under retry storms. Patch deployed 2026-03-13; monitoring shows stable behavior.
next_steps: 1) Complete comprehensive audit of KV cache eviction logic and add unit/integration tests to prevent re-emission races (owner: runtime-team, due 2026-04-01).
2) Improve FD monitoring and add automatic circuit-breaker when per-node open-FD exceeds safe threshold (owner: infra-sre, due 2026-03-25).
3) Update runbook for dedicated pools to include immediate steps for memory/FD pressure (owner: support-docs, due 2026-03-20).
4) Share finalized postmortem with HelixBank security/compliance and include list of config changes (owner: CS, due 2026-03-16).
5) Add regression tests in staging that simulate client retry storms with KV cache enabled (owner: qa, due 2026-03-30).
